title: Each finished job writes one operations row with its queue wait, lock wait and run time, and kbjob.py stats prints their medians per operation
goal: the executor records one ops row job.run per finished job in the query log's ops store (closed keys: op, exit class, attempt, queued_ms, wait_ms of waiting-lock and waiting-merge, run_ms), through ql_capture as land.step rows are, and kbjob.py stats prints for each operation one line op n=N queued_ms=MEDIAN wait_ms=MEDIAN run_ms=MEDIAN (nearest-rank p95 beside it), so the wait the service removes from a session is measured the same way backlog.py landings measures a landing

run: import sys,os,tempfile,subprocess; d=tempfile.mkdtemp(); env=dict(os.environ,CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA=d,CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=os.getcwd(),KB_HOST_LOCK_DIR=d); s=os.path.join(d,"c.sqlite"); kb=lambda *x: subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/kbjob.py","--store",s,*x],env=env,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=300); assert kb("submit","check","--name","backlog-check","--no-ensure").returncode==0; assert kb("serve","--once").returncode in (0,1); r=kb("stats"); assert r.returncode==0 and r.stdout.split()[0]=="check" and "run_ms" in r.stdout and "queued_ms" in r.stdout, r
